option_description: Controls the formally assigned data sensitivity classification label for the media files asset, indicating whether it has been reviewed and labeled by a data governance or privacy process. Determines which downstream controls — encryption, access restrictions, retention schedules, and disposal procedures — are applied to the asset.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'undefined_sensitivity_classification' when personal_data_indicator is true and this label is 'unclassified' or 'pending_review', or is absent entirely. Additionally, 'absent_or_undefined_retention_schedule', 'inadequate_access_control_granularity', 'missing_data_at_rest_encryption', and 'insecure_or_incomplete_data_disposal' all branch on specific label values. An unclassified or absent label means no downstream protective control can be consistently scoped, leaving media files containing faces, voices, or location metadata without any enforcement boundary.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to your data catalog (e.g., Collibra, Alation, Microsoft Purview) and search for the media files asset by name or storage path. Check the 'Classification' or 'Sensitivity Label' field on the asset detail page.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Data Catalog UI → Assets → Search '<asset name or storage path>' → Asset Detail → Classification / Sensitivity Label field
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A label such as 'confirmed_pii', 'possible_pii', 'confirmed_non_pii', 'pending_review', or 'unclassified' displayed on the asset record.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the data governance platform API (e.g., Microsoft Purview Information Protection REST API) to retrieve the classification label assigned to the storage account or blob container hosting the media files.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON field returning the classification string, e.g., 'confirmed_pii' or null if no label has been applied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the AWS Macie CLI to list findings for the S3 bucket or object prefix storing media files, which reveals whether Macie has auto-classified the content as containing personal data.
how_to_obtain.command: aws macie2 list-findings --finding-criteria '{"criterion":{"resourcesAffected.s3Bucket.name":{"eq":["<bucket-name>"]}}}' --query 'findingIds' | xargs -I{} aws macie2 get-findings --finding-ids {} --query 'findings[].classificationDetails.result.sensitiveData'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of sensitive data categories detected (e.g., PERSONAL_INFORMATION, FINANCIAL, CREDENTIALS) or an empty array if none found, informing the appropriate label value.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the data owner or data steward responsible for the media files asset and review any Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) or data inventory spreadsheet that references this asset. Confirm whether a formal classification review has been completed and documented.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Written confirmation of classification status in a DPIA, data register, or governance ticket, or acknowledgement that no formal review has occurred (indicating 'unclassified').

option_description: Controls whether the media files asset is flagged as known or suspected to contain personal information such as PII or PHI. This is set based on data discovery scans, schema analysis, or explicit data owner attestation. A true value means that personal data is present or possibly present in the stored media.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'undefined_sensitivity_classification' only when personal_data_indicator is true and the sensitivity label is 'unclassified', 'pending_review', or absent. If this flag is incorrectly set to false or left null, the rule will not trigger even if media files contain facial images, voice recordings, or location-embedded metadata — silently bypassing the classification enforcement gate. Accurate population of this flag is the prerequisite for all downstream exposure checks.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run a DLP scan using open-source tools such as bulk_extractor or Microsoft Presidio against a sample of the media files to detect embedded personal identifiers (EXIF GPS coordinates, faces, speech transcripts).
how_to_obtain.command: python3 -c "import presidio_analyzer; from presidio_analyzer import AnalyzerEngine; engine = AnalyzerEngine(); results = engine.analyze(text=open('/mnt/media_sample/transcript.txt').read(), language='en'); print(results)"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of recognized entity types such as PERSON, LOCATION, PHONE_NUMBER, or EMAIL_ADDRESS found in extracted text or metadata, confirming personal data presence.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect EXIF metadata from image and video media files using exiftool to identify embedded GPS coordinates, device owner names, or other personal identifiers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CSV output showing populated GPS, Author, or Artist fields, which confirms personal data is embedded in the media and the indicator should be set to true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the DLP platform API (e.g., Google Cloud DLP) to inspect stored media file samples and retrieve findings that indicate personal data presence.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A DLP job results table populated with finding counts per info type, indicating which media files contain personal data identifiers.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review data owner attestation records, privacy registration forms, or Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) to determine whether the media files asset has been formally declared as containing personal information.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A signed attestation or RoPA entry confirming personal data presence or absence, or absence of any record indicating the indicator has never been formally evaluated.

option_description: Controls whether a documented and actively enforced retention period exists for the media files asset. A true value requires that a formal retention schedule has been written, approved, and operationally applied — not merely referenced in a general policy document.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'absent_or_undefined_retention_schedule' when retention_schedule_defined is false (or absent) and the sensitivity label is 'confirmed_pii', 'possibly_pii', or 'unclassified'. It also fires when retention_schedule_defined is true but retention_enforcement_mechanism is 'none', indicating schedule-on-paper without technical implementation. For media files that accumulate indefinitely — video surveillance footage, recorded calls, user-uploaded images — the absence of a defined schedule means personal data is retained beyond lawful purpose, breaching GDPR Article 5(1)(e) and creating growing exposure windows. This attribute also gates the 'insecure_or_incomplete_data_disposal' rule.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the data catalog or data governance platform for a retention policy linked to this media files asset. In Microsoft Purview, navigate to Data Catalog → Browse Assets → select the media asset → 'Policies' or 'Retention' tab.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft Purview → Data Catalog → Assets → '<media asset name>' → Policies tab → Retention Period field
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A defined retention duration (e.g., '90 days', '7 years') and a reference to the governing policy document, confirming the schedule is formally established.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the records retention schedule document or data management policy stored in the organization's policy repository (e.g., SharePoint, Confluence) for entries covering media file categories.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rows listing the media data category, retention period, and review date, confirming a schedule exists. No matching rows indicates the schedule is undefined.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the cloud storage lifecycle policy API to verify whether a retention rule has been applied to the bucket or container storing media files.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON list of lifecycle rules with 'Expiration' or 'Transition' entries showing the configured retention period. An empty response or 'NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration' error indicates no schedule is defined.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the data steward or records manager to verify whether a retention schedule covering media files has been formally approved, documented in a register, and communicated to operational teams responsible for enforcement.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A reference to a documented and approved retention schedule entry covering this asset class, or confirmation that no such schedule currently exists.

option_description: Controls how the retention policy for the media files asset is technically enforced. Distinguishes between automated deletion (data is purged by a system process at schedule expiry), automated archival (data is moved to cold/archival storage), manual documented process (a person follows a checklist), and none (no enforcement mechanism exists despite any declared schedule).
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'absent_or_undefined_retention_schedule' not only when no schedule is defined but also when retention_schedule_defined is true yet retention_enforcement_mechanism is 'none'. This captures the common gap where a retention policy exists on paper but has never been technically implemented. For media files — which can grow to petabyte scale — a manual_documented_process is also high-risk unless audited regularly, as human error or staff turnover can cause it to lapse silently. Automated enforcement is the only reliable control for large-scale persistent media storage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect S3 bucket lifecycle configuration to determine whether automated deletion or archival rules are active and properly configured for the media storage bucket.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket <media-bucket-name> | jq '{rules: [.Rules[] | {id: .ID, status: .Status, expiration_days: .Expiration.Days, transition_storage_class: .Transitions[0].StorageClass, transition_days: .Transitions[0].Days}]}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rules showing 'Status: Enabled' with either 'Expiration.Days' (automated_deletion) or 'Transitions' with a storage class (automated_archival). Empty output or disabled rules maps to 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for scheduled deletion or archival jobs in cron, systemd timers, or cloud scheduler services that target the media storage path.
how_to_obtain.command: crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -i -E 'media|video|audio|delete|purge|archive'; systemctl list-timers --all | grep -i -E 'media|purge|archive|retention'; gcloud scheduler jobs list --format='table(name,schedule,state)' 2>/dev/null | grep -i media
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A scheduled job entry showing a cron expression, a target path matching the media storage location, and an active/enabled status, confirming automated_deletion or automated_archival. No output maps to 'none' or requires manual process investigation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management policies defined in JSON configuration files or ARM/Bicep templates for the storage account hosting media files.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A policy rule with 'enabled: true' and an action containing 'delete.daysAfterModificationGreaterThan' or 'tierToCool.daysAfterModificationGreaterThan', confirming automated enforcement. Missing or disabled rules map to 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review SOPs, runbooks, or decommissioning checklists for documented manual retention enforcement procedures that explicitly reference media files, including responsible owner, frequency, and evidence of last execution.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A runbook with a signed execution log showing dates when media files were reviewed and deleted/archived per schedule, confirming 'manual_documented_process'. Absence of such records and no automated mechanism maps to 'none'.

option_description: Controls which access control paradigm is applied to the media files asset. Options span from fine-grained controls (rbac_scoped: roles scoped to specific data functions; abac_scoped: attribute-based policies considering data sensitivity, user context, and purpose) through to weak controls (shared_credentials: a single username/password used by multiple people; overpermissioned_role: a role granting access broader than necessary; none: no access policy defined).
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'inadequate_access_control_granularity' when sensitivity_classification_label is absent and access_control_model is 'shared_credentials', 'overpermissioned_role', or 'none'. It also fires when the classification label is set but authorized_roles_defined is false alongside a weak access model. For media files, shared credentials are particularly dangerous because audit trails for individual access events are destroyed — meaning a data breach involving personal images or voice recordings cannot be attributed to a specific actor. The 'none' model leaves media openly accessible to any authenticated principal on the platform.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate IAM policies attached to the S3 bucket or object prefix hosting media files to determine whether access is scoped by role, uses wildcard principals, or is attached to overly broad managed policies.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <media-bucket-name> | jq '.Policy | fromjson | .Statement[] | {principals: .Principal, actions: .Action, effect: .Effect, conditions: .Condition}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Statements showing specific IAM role ARNs as principals with limited s3:GetObject or s3:PutObject actions and condition keys (rbac_scoped/abac_scoped), versus wildcard '*' principal or AWS account root (overpermissioned_role/none).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Azure RBAC role assignments on the storage container or blob path hosting media files to identify whether fine-grained roles (e.g., Storage Blob Data Reader) or broad roles (e.g., Contributor, Owner) are applied.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A table listing principals with 'Storage Blob Data Reader' or custom scoped roles (rbac_scoped), versus 'Contributor' or 'Owner' assignments (overpermissioned_role), or an empty table (none).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the GCS bucket permissions page in the Google Cloud Console to identify whether access is granted via fine-grained IAM bindings, uniform bucket-level access with role-based principals, or public/allUsers entries.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Google Cloud Console → Cloud Storage → Buckets → '<media bucket>' → Permissions tab → View by Principals
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of principals with specific IAM roles (e.g., roles/storage.objectViewer) bound to service accounts or groups (rbac_scoped), versus allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers (none/overpermissioned), or a single service account used by all consumers (shared_credentials).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the platform or storage administrator to determine whether shared service account credentials are distributed to multiple teams for media file access, or whether individual identity-bound roles are enforced.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirmation that each team or function accesses media files via individually provisioned identities with scoped permissions (rbac_scoped/abac_scoped), or disclosure that a shared access key or service account password is used by multiple parties (shared_credentials).

option_description: Controls whether an explicit, documented allowlist of roles or principals authorized to access the media files asset exists, scoped to minimum necessary access for each function. A true value requires that the allowlist is formal, current, and role-scoped per function — not merely a department-level or organization-wide group assignment.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'inadequate_access_control_granularity' when sensitivity_classification_label is absent and authorized_roles_defined is false. It also fires when the label is set but authorized_roles_defined is false in combination with a weak access_control_model. Without an explicit role allowlist for media files, there is no authoritative reference against which IAM drift can be measured — meaning roles that accumulate access over time (joiner/mover/leaver failures) cannot be detected during access reviews. This is particularly critical for media files containing biometric data or surveillance footage, where unauthorized access may not be immediately evident from usage logs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Locate the data access matrix, authorization register, or IAM policy document in the organization's governance repository that lists approved roles for the media files asset. Verify it is tied to a specific asset identifier and not a general storage policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rows or entries listing specific role names (e.g., 'media-analyst-read', 'surveillance-admin-write') scoped to the media files asset, with an owner and review date. Absence indicates authorized_roles_defined should be set to false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the IAM system API to list all principals and roles with access to the media storage resource, then cross-reference against a documented access register to determine if assignments match an approved allowlist.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam list-entities-for-policy --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::<account>:policy/<MediaFilesAccessPolicy> --query '{roles: PolicyRoles[*].RoleName, groups: PolicyGroups[*].GroupName, users: PolicyUsers[*].UserName}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A bounded list of roles, groups, and users attached to the media access policy. If this list cannot be reconciled against a documented authorized roles register, authorized_roles_defined should be false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the data governance platform (e.g., Collibra, Atlan), open the media files asset record and navigate to the 'Access Policy' or 'Authorized Users' section to check for a formally defined and maintained roles list.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Collibra → Data Catalog → '<media asset>' → Access Control → Authorized Roles / Data Access Policy section
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A populated list of named roles with function-level justifications and an approval date, confirming authorized_roles_defined is true. An empty or missing section confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request the most recent access review report or certification record for the media files asset from the identity governance team, verifying that role assignments have been formally approved and are scoped to minimum necessary access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A signed access review report listing certified roles and principals with access to the media asset, dated within the required review cycle. Absence of such a report indicates authorized_roles_defined is false.

typical_values: false (most common — access rarely formally documented for media)
true (present in regulated environments with access certification programs)

option_description: Controls whether the persistent storage layer hosting the media files — including disks, object storage volumes, or NAS shares — has encryption at rest mandated and verified as actively applied. This must be confirmed as enforced through configuration evidence, not merely available or default-enabled in theory.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'missing_data_at_rest_encryption' when sensitivity_classification_label is 'unclassified' or 'pending_review' and encryption_at_rest_enabled is false, and also when encryption_policy_mandated is true but encryption is not enabled. For media files — which may contain facial recognition source images, biometric voice samples, or surveillance recordings — unencrypted persistent storage means that any actor with physical access to the storage medium, or logical access bypassing application-layer controls, can read the content in plaintext. This is especially relevant for cloud object storage where snapshot exports or cross-region replication copies may inadvertently exist without encryption.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether server-side encryption is enforced on the S3 bucket containing media files, including the encryption algorithm and whether a bucket policy denies unencrypted PutObject requests.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket <media-bucket-name> --query 'ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration.Rules[*].{Algorithm:ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.SSEAlgorithm,KMSKeyID:ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.KMSMasterKeyID,BucketKeyEnabled:BucketKeyEnabled}'; aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <media-bucket-name> | jq '.Policy | fromjson | .Statement[] | select(.Condition.StringNotEquals["s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption"] != null)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output showing 'SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms' or 'AES256' with a bucket policy statement denying requests where server-side encryption is not set, confirming encryption is enforced. 'ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError' or missing deny policy indicates encryption_at_rest_enabled is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify Azure Storage Account encryption settings for the account hosting media files, confirming that encryption is enabled and that customer-managed keys (CMK) are applied if required by policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'encryption_enabled: true' with 'key_source: Microsoft.Storage' (platform-managed) or 'Microsoft.Keyvault' (customer-managed), confirming active encryption. 'encryption_enabled: false' confirms encryption_at_rest_enabled is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Terraform or CloudFormation infrastructure-as-code templates that provision the media file storage resources to verify that encryption configuration is explicitly declared and not relying on default behavior.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IaC blocks showing explicit encryption configuration (e.g., 'server_side_encryption_configuration' with 'sse_algorithm = "aws:kms"' in Terraform), confirming encryption is codified as enforced. Absence or commented-out blocks indicates reliance on defaults that may not be verified.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the Google Cloud Storage bucket configuration in the Console to verify that a Cloud KMS key is assigned for encryption, or that Google-managed encryption is confirmed as active.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Google Cloud Console → Cloud Storage → Buckets → '<media bucket>' → Configuration tab → Encryption section
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'Google-managed key' or a specific Cloud KMS key URI displayed in the Encryption section, confirming encryption at rest is active. A missing or unconfigured section warrants CLI verification.

typical_values: true (default in major cloud providers for new buckets, but not always enforced by policy)
false (common for legacy NAS, on-premises media archives, or misconfigured object storage)

option_description: Controls whether an organizational data protection policy, security baseline, or regulatory compliance framework (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) explicitly requires encryption at rest for data assets that may contain personal information or that are unclassified. This is a policy-layer attribute distinct from whether encryption is technically implemented.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'missing_data_at_rest_encryption' when encryption_policy_mandated is true but encryption_at_rest_enabled is false — capturing the critical gap where a policy mandate exists but has not been technically fulfilled. For media files, this scenario is common when security baselines are updated to require encryption for all PII-adjacent storage, but legacy media repositories pre-dating the policy have not been remediated. Even when a policy mandate exists, without technical enforcement it provides no actual protection. This attribute also serves as the bridge between compliance requirements and technical control validation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the organization's data protection or information security policy documents, security baseline standards, or compliance framework mappings to identify explicit requirements for encryption at rest covering media files or unclassified data assets.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -i -E 'encrypt.*rest|at.rest.*encrypt|media.*encrypt|unclassified.*encrypt|pii.*encrypt' /path/to/security_policy.pdf 2>/dev/null || find /path/to/policies/ -name '*.pdf' -o -name '*.docx' | xargs grep -il 'encryption at rest' 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy text containing explicit language such as 'all data assets containing or potentially containing personal data must be encrypted at rest' or 'unclassified assets pending review must apply encryption controls', confirming encryption_policy_mandated is true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In a GRC platform (e.g., ServiceNow GRC, OneTrust, Vanta), navigate to the applicable compliance framework mapping to locate controls that mandate encryption at rest for the media files asset classification tier.
how_to_obtain.navigation: GRC Platform → Compliance → Frameworks → '<GDPR / HIPAA / PCI-DSS>' → Control Mapping → Search 'encryption at rest' → Review applicability to data asset class
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A mapped control entry (e.g., GDPR Article 32, HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv), PCI-DSS Requirement 3.5) marked as applicable to this asset class, with an owner and implementation status, confirming encryption_policy_mandated is true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query AWS Config or Azure Policy to determine whether a policy rule mandating storage encryption is assigned and in scope for the media storage accounts or buckets.
how_to_obtain.command: aws configservice describe-config-rules --query 'ConfigRules[?contains(ConfigRuleName,`encrypt`) == `true`].{Name:ConfigRuleName,Scope:Scope,State:ConfigRuleState}'; az policy assignment list --query '[?contains(name,`encrypt`) || contains(displayName,`ncrypt`)].{name:name,displayName:displayName,enforcementMode:enforcementMode,scope:scope}' -o table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active Config rules or Policy assignments with names containing 'encrypt' applied to the storage scope, in 'ACTIVE' or 'Enforce' state, confirming a technical policy mandate exists. No matching rules indicates encryption_policy_mandated may be false or only exist in documentation without technical enforcement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Consult the Data Protection Officer or CISO office to confirm whether the organization's information security policy, data classification standard, or applicable regulatory obligations formally require encryption at rest for media files in this classification tier.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A written confirmation referencing the specific policy document section, version, and date that mandates encryption at rest for this asset type, or acknowledgement that no such mandate currently exists in formal policy.

typical_values: true (required by GDPR Article 32, HIPAA, PCI-DSS for PII/PHI-adjacent storage)
false (common in organizations without a formal data classification-linked security baseline)
null (not yet assessed against applicable regulatory requirements)

option_description: Controls whether media files containing or possibly containing personal information have been processed through anonymization or pseudonymization techniques — such as face blurring, metadata stripping, tokenization of embedded identifiers, or differential privacy mechanisms — prior to or at the point of persistent storage.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers the 'absent_anonymization_or_pseudonymization_controls' exposure when this attribute is false or absent AND either the sensitivity classification is 'confirmed_pii', 'possible_pii', or 'unclassified', OR no privacy-by-design assessment has been completed. For media files, the risk is particularly acute because EXIF metadata, embedded GPS coordinates, facial biometrics, and audio identifiers are often overlooked as personal data vectors. A false or null value here means individuals remain identifiable in stored media, violating GDPR Recital 26 privacy-by-design principles.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect media file EXIF/metadata to detect unstripped personal identifiers such as GPS coordinates, device serial numbers, or author fields, which would indicate anonymization has NOT been applied.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If anonymization is applied, GPS fields should be absent or zeroed, author/creator fields should be blank or tokenized. Presence of real GPS coordinates or personal identifiers indicates anonymization_pseudonymization_applied = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review ETL/media processing pipeline configuration files for anonymization transform steps such as face blurring, metadata scrubbing, or PII redaction stages applied before storage.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration files referencing blur, redact, strip-exif, or anonymize stages confirm the attribute is true. Absence of such references indicates the attribute should be set to false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the data governance or media processing platform API to retrieve the processing manifest for this media asset class, confirming whether anonymization transforms are registered.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON response listing anonymization or pseudonymization transform entries confirms true. An empty array or 404 indicates false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the data engineering or media processing team to determine whether a formal anonymization step is documented in the media ingestion runbook, and request evidence of the last execution log showing PII scrubbing was performed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A runbook entry describing metadata stripping or face-blurring with an associated execution log confirms true. No documented step or log confirms false.

option_description: Indicates whether a formal Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) or privacy-by-design review has been completed and documented for the media files data asset, explicitly evaluating whether anonymization and pseudonymization controls are required and applied.
security_impact: The Rego policy uses this attribute as a secondary trigger for 'absent_anonymization_or_pseudonymization_controls': when both privacy_by_design_assessment_completed is false/absent AND anonymization_pseudonymization_applied is false/absent, the exposure fires regardless of sensitivity classification. For media files, a DPIA is critical because media content is a non-obvious carrier of biometric, locational, and behavioral personal data. Without a completed assessment, decisions about masking, metadata scrubbing, and consent-based processing have likely never been formally made, leaving the asset in an uncontrolled state.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request the data governance or privacy team's DPIA register and confirm whether an assessment entry exists for the 'Media Files' data asset, including the date completed, assessor name, and whether anonymization controls were explicitly evaluated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A DPIA register entry with asset name 'Media Files', completion date, and a section addressing anonymization/pseudonymization decisions confirms true. Absence of any entry confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to the privacy management platform (e.g., OneTrust, TrustArc, or internal GRC tool) and search for a DPIA record associated with the media files asset or its owning system.
how_to_obtain.navigation: OneTrust: Privacy Program > Assessments > Search 'Media Files' or parent system name > Filter by Type=DPIA > Check Status=Completed. TrustArc: Data Inventory > [Asset Name] > Assessments tab > Confirm DPIA status.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A DPIA record with status 'Completed' and explicit reference to media file processing confirms true. Status 'In Progress', 'Not Started', or no record confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for a DPIA completion artifact file in the project or asset documentation repository, which may be stored as a PDF, Word document, or structured YAML/JSON assessment record.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A file matching the pattern with a modification date and 'completed' or 'approved' status within the document confirms true. No matching file confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the GRC or privacy management system API to retrieve assessment records linked to the media files asset class.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${GRC_API_TOKEN}' '${GRC_API_BASE}/api/assessments?asset_class=media_files&type=dpia&status=completed' | jq '{count: .total, latest: .results[0] | {id, completed_date, assessor, anonymization_evaluated}}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A response with count > 0 and a completed_date value confirms true. A count of 0 or empty results confirms false.

option_description: Controls whether technical enforcement mechanisms — such as cloud region locking, geo-restriction policies, CDN origin rules, or storage bucket location constraints — are actively preventing or governing the movement of media files across national or regulatory jurisdictions.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires the 'non_compliant_cross_border_transfer' exposure when cross_border_transfer_mechanism is 'none' AND data_residency_controls_enforced is false. For media files, cloud object storage is the predominant backend, and without explicit region locking, replication policies may silently copy files to geographically distributed nodes in non-compliant jurisdictions. A false value here means personal data embedded in media — facial images, voice recordings, GPS-tagged photos — may cross borders without legal basis, violating GDPR Chapter V and similar cross-border data transfer regulations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS S3-backed media storage, check whether bucket replication rules are absent or restricted to compliant regions, and confirm the bucket's region matches the required residency jurisdiction.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-location --bucket ${MEDIA_BUCKET_NAME} && aws s3api get-bucket-replication --bucket ${MEDIA_BUCKET_NAME} 2>&1 | jq '{location: .LocationConstraint, replication: .ReplicationConfiguration.Rules[].Destination.Bucket}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: LocationConstraint should match the required jurisdiction region (e.g., 'eu-west-1' for EU residency). Replication rules should either be absent or restricted to same-jurisdiction buckets. Cross-region replication to non-compliant regions confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Azure Blob Storage, verify that the storage account is locked to the required region and that geo-redundant storage (GRS) or cross-region replication has been disabled or restricted.
how_to_obtain.command: az storage account show --name ${STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME} --resource-group ${RG_NAME} --query '{location: location, replicationMode: sku.name, allowCrossTenantReplication: allowCrossTenantReplication}' -o json
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Location should be the required residency region. sku.name should be 'Standard_LRS' or 'Premium_LRS' (locally redundant) rather than 'Standard_GRS' or 'Standard_RAGRS' for strict residency. allowCrossTenantReplication should be false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the cloud provider console, navigate to the media storage bucket or container settings and confirm region, replication, and any geo-restriction policies applied.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console: S3 > [Bucket Name] > Properties > AWS Region (confirm) + Management > Replication rules (confirm absent or region-restricted). GCP Console: Cloud Storage > [Bucket] > Configuration > Location type (confirm single-region). Azure Portal: Storage Accounts > [Account] > Configuration > Replication.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Single-region deployment with no cross-region replication rules, or explicit geo-restriction policies referencing the required jurisdiction, confirms true. Multi-region or unrestricted replication confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, CloudFormation, or Pulumi) configurations for the media storage resources to confirm explicit region constraints and absence of cross-region replication.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Region or location variable set to the required jurisdiction with no replication blocks targeting other regions confirms true. Absent region constraint or active cross-region replication blocks confirm false.

option_description: Identifies the specific legal instrument — adequacy decision, Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs), derogation, or none — that authorizes the transfer of personal data embedded in media files across national or regulatory jurisdictions.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'non_compliant_cross_border_transfer' when this attribute is set to 'none' and either data_residency_controls_enforced is false, or sensitivity_classification_label is absent. For media files distributed via CDNs, processed by third-party transcoding services, or backed up to geographically distributed cloud infrastructure, cross-border transfer is a near-certain occurrence. A value of 'none' with no residency controls means personal data in media files may be transferred internationally without any legally recognized mechanism, constituting a direct GDPR Chapter V violation and exposing the organization to regulatory enforcement action.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request the data processing register (Article 30 record) and DPA/vendor agreement inventory from the legal or privacy team, and identify whether any SCCs, adequacy decisions, or BCR references are documented for media file transfers involving international vendors or cloud providers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An Article 30 record entry for media files with a named transfer mechanism (e.g., 'EU SCCs 2021 — Module 2' with the cloud provider) confirms the appropriate enum value. No entry or 'none' documented confirms the default 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the privacy management platform, locate the data flow or transfer record for the media files asset and identify the legal basis documented for any international data transfers.
how_to_obtain.navigation: OneTrust: Data Mapping > Data Flows > Filter by Asset='Media Files' > Cross-Border Transfers section > Legal Mechanism column. TrustArc: Data Inventory > [Asset] > Transfer Details > Legal Basis for Transfer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented mechanism of 'Standard Contractual Clauses', 'Adequacy Decision', 'Binding Corporate Rules', or 'Derogation' confirms the corresponding enum value. Blank or 'None' confirms 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check DPA (Data Processing Agreement) documents or legal contract archives for executed SCCs or BCR acceptance records linked to media file processing vendors such as CDN providers, cloud storage, or transcoding services.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An executed SCC, BCR acceptance letter, or adequacy-based DPA referencing media file transfers confirms the corresponding enum value. No matching documents confirm 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the legal or contract management system API for transfer mechanism records associated with the media files asset or its data controllers/processors.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${LEGAL_API_TOKEN}' '${LEGAL_API_BASE}/api/v1/transfers?asset=media_files' | jq '.transfers[] | {mechanism: .legal_basis, jurisdiction: .destination_jurisdiction, status: .status, executed_date: .execution_date}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Records with legal_basis values of 'standard_contractual_clauses', 'adequacy_decision', 'binding_corporate_rules', or 'derogation' with status 'active' confirm the corresponding enum value. Empty results or 'none' status confirms 'none'.

option_description: Indicates whether a formally documented end-of-life disposal procedure — covering secure deletion, media sanitization, crypto-shredding, or equivalent — has been explicitly defined and assigned to the media files data asset, including coverage of all backup and archive copies.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'insecure_or_incomplete_data_disposal' when the asset has a 'classified' sensitivity label with a defined retention schedule but no disposal_procedure_defined. Media files present a uniquely difficult disposal challenge because they exist across multiple storage tiers — primary object storage, CDN edge caches, transcoded derivative copies, backup snapshots, and offline tape archives. A false or null value means personal data in media files may persist on decommissioned storage media, in forgotten archive repositories, or in backup snapshots beyond authorized retention periods, creating residual exposure to physical exfiltration and regulatory liability.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request the data management runbook and decommissioning checklist from the infrastructure or data governance team, and verify whether a named disposal procedure explicitly references the media files asset class, including its backup and archive locations.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A runbook section titled or tagged for media files disposal, specifying methods such as crypto-shredding of S3 bucket keys, DoD 5220.22-M wipe of NAS volumes, or tape degaussing, confirms true. Generic or absent disposal procedures confirm false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search documentation repositories and runbook directories for disposal or decommissioning procedures that explicitly mention media files, video, audio, images, or associated storage systems.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more procedure files referencing both disposal methods and media file asset types confirms true. No matching files confirm false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether automated lifecycle policies with expiration actions are configured on the primary media storage backend, which may serve as the technical implementation of a disposal procedure.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket ${MEDIA_BUCKET_NAME} 2>/dev/null | jq '.Rules[] | {id: .ID, status: .Status, expiration: .Expiration, noncurrent_expiration: .NoncurrentVersionExpiration, abort_multipart: .AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lifecycle rules with Expiration.Days set and Status='Enabled' indicate an automated disposal mechanism exists. However, confirm this is formally documented — automated rules alone without documentation may not fully confirm true. No lifecycle rules confirm false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the GRC or data governance tool, locate the data asset record for media files and check the lifecycle or disposal section for a formally assigned disposal procedure with an owner and last-review date.
how_to_obtain.navigation: ServiceNow: Data Asset Registry > Media Files > Lifecycle tab > Disposal Procedure field. Collibra: Data Assets > [Media Files] > Governance > End-of-Life Procedure. Custom GRC: Data Inventory > [Asset] > Disposal & Retention section.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A named disposal procedure with an assigned owner, applicable methods, and coverage of backup/archive copies confirms true. An empty or 'Not Defined' field confirms false.
